title: What Should World Models Plan Over? Learning Geometry-Aligned Representations of Body Motion
abstract: arXiv:2611.29759v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We introduce MotionPort, which learns low-dimensional latent representations of body motion for accurate dynamics prediction and effective long-horizon planning. Existing world-model planners often search over action representations learned for prediction, yet we show that predictive accuracy alone does not ensure that optimization can discover successful trajectories. MotionPort addresses this mismatch by representing body trajectories rather than action chunks and organizing the search space by motion similarity, helping predicted improvements translate into successful execution. Without fine-tuning state encoders, MotionPort raises average goal-reaching success from 37.9% to 87.8% across three backbones and seven settings in four domains. On the evaluated AntMaze-OGBench tasks, it achieves 72% success, compared with 4% for the strongest baseline.

translated_title: 世界模型应该规划什么？学习几何对齐的身体运动表征
translated_abstract: 我们提出了MotionPort，它学习身体运动的低维潜在表征，以实现准确的动力学预测和有效的长时程规划。现有的世界模型规划器通常在为预测而学习的动作表征上进行搜索，然而我们表明，仅凭预测准确性并不能保证优化过程能够发现成功的轨迹。MotionPort通过以身体轨迹（而非动作块）作为表征，并按运动相似性组织搜索空间来解决这一不匹配问题，从而使预测的改进能够转化为成功的执行。在无需微调状态编码器的情况下，MotionPort在四个领域的三个骨干网络和七种设置中，将平均目标达成成功率从37.9%提升至87.8%。在所评估的AntMaze-OGBench任务上，它达到了72%的成功率，而最强基线仅为4%。
tldr: MotionPort通过学习几何对齐的身体轨迹表征并按运动相似性组织规划搜索空间，将世界模型规划器的平均目标达成成功率从37.9%大幅提升至87.8%。
en_tdlr: MotionPort learns geometry-aligned representations of body trajectories and organizes the planning search space by motion similarity, dramatically raising average goal-reaching success of world-model planners from 37.9% to 87.8%.
